purpose: IV Fat Emulsion is a liquid nutrition given directly into your vein when you cannot eat normally or get enough nutrition by mouth. It provides your body with healthy fats and calories to keep you energized and help your organs function properly. It is also used to provide essential fatty acids that your body cannot make on its own.
how_it_works: This medication is made from plant-based oils, like soybean or olive oil, mixed with water to create a milky liquid that is safe to put into your bloodstream. Your body breaks down these tiny fat droplets just like the fats you would normally digest from food. This gives your cells the energy and building blocks they need to stay healthy, especially when you are too sick to eat.
common_side_effects: Fever, chills, or a warm feeling during the infusion. You might notice nausea, vomiting, or headache. Some people get a temporary increase in fat levels in the blood, or mild redness and irritation at the IV site.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any egg, soybean, or peanut allergies, as some formulas contain these ingredients. People with severe liver disease, kidney problems, or very high blood fat levels should use this with extra caution. Your doctor will monitor your blood regularly to make sure your body is handling the fat correctly. Do not use if the emulsion looks separated or oily — it should look smooth and milky white.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated by your doctor or pharmacist based on your weight, age, and medical needs. It is given slowly through an IV, usually over several hours each day. Most adults receive around 1 to 2 grams of fat per kilogram of body weight per day, but your care team will set the exact amount that is right for you.
